page: Amazon Web Services c8id.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running at 3.9 GHz. The system includes 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 5700 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-threaded and memory-intensive operations. The instance achieved a Passmark CPU score of 106,825.4 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 22,327.0, both placing in the top tier. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 7,652.04 GB/sec and large block uncached speeds at 362.34 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang also registered in the top tier. However, single-core performance is relatively moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average to strong categories.

The c8id.24xlarge is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads, database operations, and high-throughput web serving. It achieved 166.59 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 159.75 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. The inclusion of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) supports prompt processing for large language models, where it achieved top-tier speeds, though text generation rates remain average. The high-density local NVMe storage and compute-to-memory ratio make it a cost-efficient option for high-performance databases and parallel processing tasks, though workloads requiring massive memory-to-vCPU ratios may find the 2.0 GB per core allocation limiting.
